doc.title: Ken Poston interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 4, 2024

chapter: Jazz today and the business of events
title: Sponsorship, audiences and streaming making events harder
summary: He relies on audience attendance rather than sponsors, and says streaming, Zoom and Covid make radio and events harder.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: Yeah. As a producer of events is part of your task to go out and find some of those people and companies to subsidize these concerts?

It should be but I’ve never really done it. Pretty much everything I’ve ever done is based on the audience attendance. There’s a few exceptions to that but not really anything where I had gone out and sought it out but I’ve had a couple of occasions where a sponsor has come to me. And frankly I’ve had some we’ve turned down that didn’t — that what they wanted in return for sponsorship would have altered the event or the purpose of the event. So it’s — so no, that’s not something I’ve done. It’s something that if I was smarter I would have done maybe, but never done it. I’ve always worked from a standpoint of trying to understand the audience or whatever segment of the audience that I’m going to promote something to, and find a way to get them excited about going. It’s

not that hard to find the audience. I mean we know where they are, but you’ve got to convince them in this day and age to get in the car and go somewhere and that’s harder today than it’s ever been. That was the other thing I was going to say from your earlier question is with the advent of Zoom, the advent of streaming, the advent of all these things, everything is much harder for me anyway today. Radio for example — we’re still a terrestrial radio station but people can stream and listen to anything they want to listen to at any given time, they can create their own radio stations, they can create their own playlists, they can — so to me we’ve had to alter our approach with terrestrial radio — at least we have — to make sure that we create something that gives people a reason to listen to us as opposed to just listening to whoever they want to hear at any given time. And it’s kind of the same with the events because of new technologies. I think Covid played a role in teaching people how to use Zoom and streaming and teach people how to attend an event without actually going there. Things like that. I’m not saying that’s a bad thing necessarily but it’s different. So that to me is, all those things combined are what’s different now and more challenging — at least more challenging for me.
That phrase is going to stick in my head, how to attend an event without really going.
